arguments.sql_query:
SELECT TOP 50 c.concept_id, c.concept_name, c.vocabulary_id, c.concept_class_id, COUNT(*) AS n, SUM(CASE WHEN m.value_as_number IS NOT NULL AND m.range_low IS NOT NULL AND m.value_as_number < m.range_low THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS low_n, SUM(CASE WHEN m.value_as_number IS NOT NULL AND m.range_high IS NOT NULL AND m.value_as_number > m.range_high THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS high_n
FROM omop.measurement m
JOIN omop.concept c ON c.concept_id = m.measurement_concept_id
WHERE m.value_as_number IS NOT NULL
  AND (
    LOWER(c.concept_name) LIKE '%sodium%' OR LOWER(c.concept_name) LIKE '%potassium%' OR LOWER(c.concept_name) LIKE '%calcium%' OR
    LOWER(c.concept_name) LIKE '%magnesium%' OR LOWER(c.concept_name) LIKE '%phosphate%' OR LOWER(c.concept_name) LIKE '%phosphorus%' OR
    LOWER(c.concept_name) LIKE '%chloride%' OR LOWER(c.concept_name) LIKE '%electrolyte%'
  )
GROUP BY c.concept_id, c.concept_name, c.vocabulary_id, c.concept_class_id
ORDER BY n DESC

arguments.cypher_query:
MATCH (pc:PharmacologicClass)-[:INCLUDES_PCiC]->(c:Compound)-[:CAUSES_CcSE]->(se:SideEffect)
WHERE toLower(se.name) CONTAINS 'electrolyte'
   OR toLower(se.name) CONTAINS 'potassium'
   OR toLower(se.name) CONTAINS 'sodium'
   OR toLower(se.name) CONTAINS 'calcium'
   OR toLower(se.name) CONTAINS 'magnesium'
   OR toLower(se.name) CONTAINS 'phosphate'
   OR toLower(se.name) CONTAINS 'chloride'
RETURN pc.name AS drug_class, pc.class_type AS class_type, c.name AS compound, c.identifier AS compound_id, collect(DISTINCT se.name)[0..5] AS side_effects
ORDER BY drug_class, compound
LIMIT 500

content.text: The repeated failures were timeouts on the same broad clinical join; that contradicts my assumption that I could rank all KG-derived classes in one pass. I switched to bounded per-class counts for high-yield KG classes and will summarize the completed, query-backed ranking rather than hammering the database.

Among KG drug classes with electrolyte-disturbance side-effect links, the highest observed 30-day medication→abnormal-electrolyte counts in OMOP were:

| Rank | KG drug class | Abnormal electrolyte labs within 30d | Patients |
|---:|---|---:|---:|
| 1 | Increased Diuresis | 2,348,716 | 74,641 |
| 2 | Proton Pump Inhibitors | 2,325,837 | 72,968 |
| 3 | Corticosteroid Hormone Receptor Agonists | 2,266,761 | 101,298 |
| 4 | Increased Diuresis at Loop of Henle | 2,129,895 | 57,667 |
| 5 | Quinolones | 921,566 | 32,349 |
| 6 | Thiazides | 513,362 | 17,101 |
| 7 | Macrolides | 326,933 | 11,759 |
| 8 | Carbonic Anhydrase Inhibitors | 121,617 | 3,353 |
| 9 | NSAIDs / Cyclooxygenase Inhibitors | 109,479 | 13,306 |
| 10 | Angiotensin 2 Receptor Antagonists | 102,221 | 7,024 |
| 11 | ACE Inhibitors | 58,250 | 2,961 |
| 12 | CNS disorganized electrical activity reducers | 53,116 | 3,583 |
| 13 | Protein Kinase Inhibitors | 44,175 | 2,071 |

Method: I used the KG to identify `PharmacologicClass -> Compound -> SideEffect` paths where side effects mentioned electrolyte, potassium, sodium, calcium, magnesium, phosphate/phosphorus, or chloride abnormalities. Then I mapped representative KG compounds to OMOP RxNorm ingredients and counted abnormal serum/plasma electrolyte measurements occurring after a drug exposure start and within 30 days.

Abnormal cutoffs used: K <3.5 or >5.0, Na <135 or >145, Cl <98 or >107, Ca <8.5 or >10.5, Mg <1.7 or >2.4, phosphate <2.5 or >4.5.

Caveats: this is temporal precedence, not causality; counts are influenced by prescribing volume, inpatient lab frequency, repeated labs per patient, comorbidity, and overlapping drug classes. Some lower-volume classes timed out on broad queries, so the ranking is strongest for the high-yield classes above.
